title: Maximal Rectangle
summary: Given a matrix with dimensions rows by cols containing only 0's and 1's, identify the largest rectangle composed solely of 1's and provide its area.
statement: Given a matrix with dimensions rows by cols containing only 0's and 1's, identify the largest rectangle composed solely of 1's and provide its area.
constraints: A rectangular matrix with 1–200 rows and 1–200 columns contains only the characters '0' and '1'.
Return the area of the largest axis-aligned rectangle of contiguous cells containing only '1'. It may be nonsquare. Return 0 when there are no ones; do not rearrange rows or columns.
hints: For each bottom row, record how many consecutive ones end there in every column.
Each resulting height array is a histogram; find its largest rectangle with a monotonic stack.
Reset heights at zeros. Pop taller bars when a shorter bar arrives, calculating popped_height × distance_between_smaller_boundaries; append a zero-height sentinel to flush the stack.
Keep row-to-row heights, but reset the index stack for every row. Every matrix rectangle has some bottom row and is represented by that row's histogram.
editorial: Accumulate consecutive-one column heights as rows are scanned. A monotonic stack calculates the maximum histogram area for each bottom row; each bar is pushed and popped at most once per row. The largest area across all rows is the answer. This combines a two-dimensional matrix with the existing histogram pattern, rather than duplicating its input/output contract. The independent oracle enumerates all top/bottom/left/right rectangles and uses a two-dimensional zero-count prefix table to reject any containing a zero.

tests.explanation: Rows 2–3 and columns 3–5 (one-based) form an all-one 2×3 rectangle, giving area 6.
The entire 2×3 matrix is a rectangle of ones, so its area is 6; restricting the answer to squares would give only 4.
